hints: Focus on what the formula tells you, a saturated acyclic alkane with 4 carbons would be C4H10, so what does C4H8 imply?
Start by listing the open-chain alkenes, remember but-2-ene counts as just one structural isomer even though it has cis-trans forms.
Now add the ring possibilities with no double bond, think of a 4-membered ring and a 3-membered ring with a side chain, then total them up.
walkthrough:
**Work out the degree of unsaturation**

Think of this as spotting what is missing. An alkane with 4 carbons is $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}$.

Our formula is:
$$\text{C}_4\text{H}_8$$
That is 2 hydrogens short, so one double bond OR one ring must be present.

**Draw the open-chain alkene isomers**

Keep the chain open and move the double bond and branches around. You get three different carbon skeletons:
$$\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCH}_2\text{CH}_3 \text{ (but-1-ene)}$$
$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}=\text{CHCH}_3 \text{ (but-2-ene)}$$
$$\text{CH}_2=\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)_2 \text{ (2-methylpropene)}$$
Note that cis and trans but-2-ene are stereoisomers, not structural isomers, so they count as one here.

**Draw the cyclic alkane isomers**

Now remove the double bond and close into a ring instead. With 4 carbons you can make:
$$\text{cyclobutane (4-membered ring)}$$
$$\text{methylcyclopropane (3-membered ring with a methyl group)}$$
That gives 2 more structural isomers.

**Add them together**

Lovely, now just total what you found.
$$3 \text{ alkenes} + 2 \text{ cycloalkanes} = 5 \text{ structural isomers}$$

options.A: 3 counts only the three alkenes (but-1-ene, but-2-ene, methylpropene) and forgets the question instruction to also include cyclic alkanes.
options.B: 4 usually comes from counting the 3 alkenes plus only cyclobutane, missing methylcyclopropane as a second distinct ring skeleton.
options.C: 5 is correct: 3 alkene structural isomers plus 2 cycloalkane structural isomers (cyclobutane and methylcyclopropane). Cis-trans forms of but-2-ene are not counted separately as structural isomers.
options.D: 6 comes from incorrectly counting cis-but-2-ene and trans-but-2-ene as two different structural isomers. They are stereoisomers with the same connectivity, so the structural total stays at 5.
